title: Language of Thought Shapes Output Diversity in Large Language Models
reasoning: The paper explores how the language used during an LLM's intermediate 'thinking' process impacts the diversity of its final English outputs. While it evaluates 'pluralistic alignment' using datasets like the World Values Survey (WVS) to measure variety in cultural values and orientations, it does not specifically benchmark or evaluate religion, faith, or specific ethical/moral frameworks. Instead, it uses these value-based datasets as a proxy to demonstrate that multilingual thinking expands the model's output diversity and coverage of diverse cultural perspectives.
